goal.text: The user is the clue-giver in a long charades round and wants a running record of what she has already acted out, so she can be told at the end whether she repeated a clue.

turns.text: Track the clues I act out, would you?

trigger.detail: user sets up the task at the top of the round

expected_answer.text: Got it. I'll log each clue as you act it out and flag anything you repeat.

turns.text: What was the first thing I mimed?

trigger.detail: the two-fingers clue finished and a new one began

expected_answer.text: You stepped backwards and mimed driving, hands up on an invisible steering wheel.

turns.text: Sorry, quick one — which hand did I point with?

trigger.detail: pointing and waving at a peer completed

expected_answer.text: Your right hand both times. You pointed at her, then waved goodbye with the same hand.

turns.text: Did the walking come before that or after?

trigger.detail: the walk-left, walk-right sequence closed

expected_answer.text: After it. The wave came first, then you walked off to your left and stopped.

turns.text: Mm-hm... mm, actually — both hands at the end there, or just one?

trigger.detail: backchannel turns into a question mid-answer

expected_answer.text: Both. You raised them together right after you came back across to your right.

turns.text: Just before that, my left hand — doing what?

trigger.detail: gaze left the peer she was miming at and settled on the wall behind

expected_answer.text: You lifted it to your face twice, lowering it in between, just before you began gesturing while you spoke.

turns.text: Uh, wait — same hand as the driving clue?

trigger.detail: user checks a comparison while the answer is still running

expected_answer.text: No, that one was both hands on an imaginary wheel. The face gesture was left only.

turns.text: Back to my list. That hand-over-hand sway — how long did I keep it?

trigger.detail: the long hand-over-hand sway ended and free gesturing resumed

expected_answer.text: Right hand over left, swinging side to side, for about thirty seconds from two minutes in until two thirty.

turns.text: Hold on — what have I just taken hold of?

trigger.detail: stepped sideways right and grabbed a piece of furniture

expected_answer.text: The display cabinet, with your right hand, after you swayed both arms and stepped sideways.

turns.text: Still on it, or have I let go?

trigger.detail: user checks the state of the grip mid-answer

expected_answer.text: Still holding. Your grip stays put for another four seconds before you turn to the left.

turns.text: Um, hang on — what's that I've just pointed out?

trigger.detail: turned left and pointed at something, then picked it up

expected_answer.text: A potted plant to your left. A moment later you pick it up and hold it in that hand.

turns.text: And whereabouts am I standing now?

trigger.detail: the low surface slid back out of view as she turned

expected_answer.text: Over on the right of the living area, beside the unit you grabbed. As you turned, both a window and a low table came into shot.

turns.text: That's not — sorry, I meant the one in my hand. Have I let go of it?

trigger.detail: user repairs her own previous question

expected_answer.text: Not yet. You hold on to it until about three minutes, then turn right and release it.

turns.text: And now? Something in my right hand again.

trigger.detail: a new contact with the furnishing on her right began

expected_answer.text: You are brushing the curtain. That begins just after three minutes and runs for about ten seconds.

turns.text: Mm-hm... mm, actually — was that window back in shot just then?

trigger.detail: the window leaves view for the rest of the clip

expected_answer.text: Yes, for about a second and a half around three twelve. After that it does not reappear at all.

turns.text: Right, noted. Carry on.

trigger.detail: acknowledgement over the tail of the answer

expected_answer.text: Will do. I'll keep logging each clue and tell you if one comes round twice.

turns.text: Right, back to it. What have I just bent down over?

trigger.detail: she leaned in over a low surface and touched it

expected_answer.text: A side table. You walked to it, leaned in and ran your right fingertip along the edge of a board sitting on it.

turns.text: Did I touch anything else down there?

trigger.detail: follow-up over the answer about the same lean

expected_answer.text: Yes, a houseplant on it. You brushed that with your left hand a few seconds before the fingertip touch.

turns.text: Which foot did I tap after I straightened up?

trigger.detail: turned away, walked forward and pointed a foot at the floor

expected_answer.text: Your right. You turned anticlockwise, walked a couple of paces and pointed it at the floor.

turns.text: And straight after, which hand went out?

trigger.detail: spun back clockwise and jabbed a finger out

expected_answer.text: Your left. You spun back clockwise, walked on and jabbed a finger out with that one.

turns.text: The palm thing — when did that come in?

trigger.detail: quiet stretch after the answer, user picks the thread up again

expected_answer.text: You rubbed your palms together at about four ten, right after you turned back to face everyone.

turns.text: Oh, before I forget — have I reused any clue?

trigger.detail: user closes out the running record she asked for at the start

expected_answer.text: Yes, one. The hand to the face came back at three forty, about three minutes after the first time.

turns.text: That's the one. Thanks.

trigger.detail: user signs off over the tail of the answer

expected_answer.text: No problem. I'll flag it if you start that one again.
